subject: Creative Arts
source: NaCCA Creative Arts Curriculum for Primary Schools, Basic 1–3 (September 2019)
accessibility: Read prompts and choices aloud when needed. Practical responses may use classroom materials, movement, speech or drawing.

indicators.statement: Study and talk about visual artworks produced or found in other African communities that reflect the history and culture of people in those areas in Africa.
indicators.content_standard: B3.1.1.1 Generate ideas for artistic expression from people, culture, environment and topical issues.

skills.description: Identify the subject, artistic method and evidence in a work.
Study and describe in visual arts.
Use artistic evidence to explain a choice or improvement.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. What is this work about?
options: Basket making in the community studied
Work beside a river landing
A bridge over a river
Reducing waste with reusable things
questions.answer: Basket making in the community studied
hints: Identify the action or subject at the centre.
questions.explanation: The described action centres on basket making in the community studied.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. Which detail could a learner point out in the work?
options: A bottle shape printed on a cloth bag
Small stalls lined up on the riverbank
A straight band above a winding blue line
Rows winding up from a round base
questions.answer: Rows winding up from a round base
hints: Look for a detail the example actually describes.
questions.explanation: The evidence in the example is rows winding up from a round base.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. Which method is used?
options: Repeating a cut-paper printing shape
Arranging cut shapes on a map
Joining coils to build a container
Stamping a design onto fabric
questions.answer: Joining coils to build a container
hints: Think about how the parts were made or performed.
questions.explanation: The example uses joining coils to build a container to show basket making in the community studied.

questions.stem: Which source could help a class understand a basket from another African community?
options: A guess based only on its price
A reliable explanation of its use or history
A rumour with no known source
An unrelated person's shopping list
questions.answer: A reliable explanation of its use or history
hints: Look for evidence about the work and its community.
questions.explanation: Look for evidence about the work and its community. A reliable explanation of its use or history.

questions.stem: A picture shows a market long ago. Which detail could help you learn about work there?
options: The tools in the sellers' hands
The number of corners on its label
The day you visited the picture
The colour of the museum door
questions.answer: The tools in the sellers' hands
hints: Find evidence inside the picture.
questions.explanation: Find evidence inside the picture. The tools in the sellers' hands.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. Which idea does the work suggest?
options: People use the shore as a landing place
A maker shapes fibre into a useful container
People use the riverbank for trading
Containers and bags can be used again
questions.answer: A maker shapes fibre into a useful container
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: The detail of rows winding up from a round base supports the idea that a maker shapes fibre into a useful container.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. Which source would help the class check its account?

The basket maker's account in the collection
A labelled photograph of the landing in Senegal

hints: Choose evidence about the actual subject.
questions.explanation: The closest source for this subject is the basket maker's account in the collection.

questions.stem: A class studies a basket in a collection from a Kenyan community. Its maker explains how coiling builds the sides. Which sentence describes evidence before giving an opinion?
options: Rows winding up from a round base.
Everybody will like the finished piece.
The work will win first prize.

questions.stem: A drawing shows tiny figures beside a large tree. Which part suggests the tree's size?

The paper has four corners.

questions.stem: What can you learn by looking closely at the edge of a woven basket?

The name of its next owner

questions.stem: Two people remember a festival differently. How could you learn more before making a picture or a play about it?
options: Pick the story with the most characters
Ask what each person saw and compare their accounts
Put the two dates together as one date

questions.stem: A class records a speaker explaining a work. What should it do before sharing the recording?

questions.stem: A coiled container opens at the side when lifted. What should its maker test?

questions.stem: A rough rock and a smooth bottle appear in a drawing. What is the artist showing by changing the marks on their surfaces?

It shows the artist used the most costly tools.
It guarantees that everyone will have the same feeling.
It helps show keeping waste away from a river.
questions.answer: It helps show keeping waste away from a river.
hints: Ask what this choice helps the audience notice.
questions.explanation: Using mime and a simple prop helps communicate the subject through a character carrying a waste bag back from the river.

questions.stem: Two reviewers heard the narrator differently. What should the group check?
options: Which reviewer's name comes first
How the voice sounded from their different seats
Which chair was bought most recently
Who wore a more colourful shirt
questions.answer: How the voice sounded from their different seats
hints: The position of a listener can change what is heard.
questions.explanation: The position of a listener can change what is heard. How the voice sounded from their different seats.

questions.stem: Which is a feeling a learner can support with evidence?
options: Only my feeling can be right.
The maker must feel what I feel.
I felt curious when the repeated pattern suddenly changed.
Everyone will feel exactly as I did.
questions.answer: I felt curious when the repeated pattern suddenly changed.
hints: Connect a personal response with a change you noticed.
questions.explanation: Connect a personal response with a change you noticed. I felt curious when the repeated pattern suddenly changed.

questions.stem: A dance repeats a sweeping gesture to show wind. What feedback addresses its meaning?
options: The dancers had different shoe sizes.
The programme had few pages.
The second sweep was wider, so the wind seemed stronger.
It was the third item after lunch.
questions.answer: The second sweep was wider, so the wind seemed stronger.
hints: Link a change in movement to the idea.
questions.explanation: Link a change in movement to the idea. The second sweep was wider, so the wind seemed stronger.

questions.stem: Which question checks whether a work served its purpose?
options: Did its choices help the audience understand or do what the maker intended?
Was the maker standing closest to the door?
Was it finished on the tallest desk?
Did it have more letters in its title?
questions.answer: Did its choices help the audience understand or do what the maker intended?
hints: Compare the result with the aim.
questions.explanation: Compare the result with the aim. Did its choices help the audience understand or do what the maker intended?.

questions.stem: In a school exchange about a river in Kenya, pupils devise a play. A character carries a waste bag away from the bank. Review the example or a class work about keeping waste away from a river. Describe one feature, say how it affects the work and suggest a change for the next version.
hints: Connect the detail to the idea it expresses.
questions.explanation: For example, connect a character carrying a waste bag back from the river to the idea that carrying waste away helps protect the river. Other supported choices are welcome.
